page.layout: One page of text in a single column; marginal notes in the right margin (references such as "1 Pet. 2.", "Exod. 15.", "Sap. 10.", "Apoc. 4." and "Apoc. 5."); running head at top; signature "D iij" at foot.

main_text.p: tes prædicemus illius, qui nos vocauit 1 Pet. 2. e tenebris in admirabilem suam lucem. Notum est quid Moses, quid filij Israël fecerint, cùm mare peruium toti populo iter expeditum præbuisset: quomodo diuina protecti manu, & stupendam conspicati redemtionē, more agnorum exultauerint, te liberatorem, ô Domine, te fortitudinē, & laudem suam decantantes. Exod. 15. Sed quid veterem populum, quid vetus canticum dico? Sap. 10. Nouum habemus canticum, cantici agni: id statesad mare vitreum mundi huius, & citharas Dei habetes, indefessē cum vniuersa Ecclesia canamus sedenti in throno & Agno; quoniam mactatus est, & redemit nos Deo per sanguinem suum, ex omni tribu & lingua, & populo, & natione: & fecit nos Deo nostro reges & sacerdotes, & regnabimus super terram.
Tibi, O fili Dei, mortalium amator, & bone domine, ô pacificator, ô opulente saluator, & reuera rex, creator & conditor omnium, verbum & sapientia patris, lumen & iubar patris, virtus, bra-chium,

page.notes: Marginal references are read from the scan with some uncertainty ("Apoc. 4." and "Apoc. 5." beside "mundi" and "indefessē"; "Exod. 15." and "Sap. 10." beside the lines about the song). The catchword "chium," is treated as the last line. Printed "Hvmani Generis" running head, page 53 at top.
